name: Archery Range
requires: Feudal Age and a Barracks (or a Donjon for the Sicilians)
description: Trains foot archers, Skirmishers, Cavalry Archers and Hand Cannoneers, plus a few regional archer units. It researches Thumb Ring, Parthian Tactics and, for a few civilizations, Cranequins.

name: Barracks
description: Trains and upgrades infantry such as the Militia line, Spearmen and Eagle units. A Barracks is needed before an Archery Range or Stable can be built.

name: Blacksmith
description: Researches the attack and armor upgrades for infantry, archers and cavalry. The archer attack line (Fletching, Bodkin Arrow, Bracer) also adds attack and range to towers and Castles. A Blacksmith is required before a Siege Workshop can be built.

name: Bombard Tower
requires: Bombard Tower technology at the University (needs Chemistry)
description: A gunpowder tower that fires one heavy cannonball instead of arrows. It hits very hard, with a bonus against ships, but it fires slowly and costs gold. Only some civilizations can build it.

name: Caravanserai
description: Allied Trade Carts that pass close to a Caravanserai move 20% faster and regain hit points. Players place them along long trade routes.

name: Castle
description: The main fortification. It trains the civilization's unique unit, Petards and Trebuchets, and researches the unique technologies along with Hoardings, Conscription, Sappers and Spies. It fires several arrows at once, more with units garrisoned inside, supports 20 population and cannot be converted.

name: Dock
description: Builds Fishing Ships, Transport Ships, Trade Cogs and warships, and researches the fishing and warship upgrades. It is a drop site for fish. Up to 5 Fishing Ships can garrison inside, and a garrisoned Dock shoots arrows.

name: Donjon
description: The Sicilians build Donjons instead of the Watch Tower line. A Donjon trains Serjeants and the Spearman line, and it unlocks the Archery Range and Stable in place of a Barracks. It starts shooting in the Feudal Age and gains hit points and arrows with each age. Serjeants can build Donjons as well.

name: Farm
requires: Mill (Folwark for the Poles, Settlement for the Inca, Mapuche, Muisca and Tupi)
description: One Villager works a Farm for a steady, renewable supply of food once hunt and berries run out. When the food is used up the Farm leaves a dead Farm that a Villager can rebuild, or the Mill reseeds it from the queue. Units can walk over Farms, and a Farm foundation is visible to the enemy as soon as it is placed.

name: Feitoria
description: A Portuguese trading post that produces food, wood, gold and stone over time without any workers. Each Feitoria takes up 20 population space.

name: Fish Trap
description: A water farm. Fishing Ships build and work Fish Traps, and Villagers can build them too. It gives a renewable but limited amount of food and has to be rebuilt when empty.

name: Folwark
description: The Polish version of the Mill: every Mill the Poles build turns into a Folwark. It is a 3x3 food drop site that supports 5 population. When a nearby Farm of the player is worked, the Folwark instantly collects an extra 10% of the food gathered from it.

name: Fortified Church
description: The Armenian and Georgian replacement for the Monastery. It trains Monks, holds Relics and researches the Monastery technologies, and it can also shelter Villagers and Mule Carts. Garrisoned Villagers and Relics let it shoot arrows. The first one an Armenian player builds receives a free Relic.

name: Fortified Gate
requires: Fortified Wall technology at the University
description: The upgraded Gate, unlocked by the same Fortified Wall technology. It has 4,000 hit points but keeps roughly the armor of a normal Gate. Repairing it fully costs more stone than building it.

name: Fortified Wall
requires: Fortified Wall technology at the University
description: The upgraded Stone Wall. The Fortified Wall technology at the University converts every existing Stone Wall and raises hit points to 3,000 with much higher armor.

name: Gate
description: A stone gate built into a Stone Wall. Friendly units pass through and enemies are kept out, and it can be locked. Gates cannot be converted.

name: Guard Tower
requires: Guard Tower technology at the University
description: The Castle Age upgrade of the Watch Tower, researched at the University. It has more hit points, armor and attack, and the upgrade costs no stone.

name: Harbor
description: The Malay unique technology Thalassocracy turns every Dock into a Harbor. A Harbor does everything a Dock does and also shoots arrows at nearby enemies, with extra damage against ships.

name: House
description: Each House adds 5 to the population limit, up to the cap of 200. The Huns cannot build Houses because they start with the maximum population room. Khmer Houses can hold 5 Villagers, and Inca Houses support 10 population.

name: Keep
description: The Imperial Age upgrade of the Guard Tower. It adds 750 hit points, 1 attack and 1 point of each armor. Keeps can hold a position or a choke point, but siege and rams destroy them quickly.

name: Krepost
description: A smaller, cheaper Castle for the Bulgarians. It trains Konniks and Petards, shoots arrows like a Castle and supports 20 population. It cannot be converted, and the only technology it researches is the Elite Konnik upgrade.

name: Lumber Camp
description: A drop site for wood, placed next to a forest so lumberjacks walk less. It researches the woodcutting upgrades Double-Bit Axe, Bow Saw and Two-Man Saw.

name: Market
requires: Feudal Age and a Mill (or Folwark or Settlement)
description: Lets players buy and sell food, wood and stone for gold, and send tribute to allies. It trains Trade Carts, which earn gold by travelling to an allied Market. Building one also shares line of sight with allies.

name: Mill
description: Villagers drop off berries, Farm food and meat at the Mill, and it researches the Farm upgrades. Building one unlocks the Farm and the Market. Players can queue Farm reseeding here so that expired Farms rebuild themselves.

name: Mining Camp
description: A drop site for gold and stone, built beside a mine. It researches the gold and stone mining upgrades.

name: Monastery
description: Trains Monks and researches the Monk upgrades. Monks bring Relics back here, and each garrisoned Relic produces a slow trickle of gold. Holding every Relic in Monasteries can win a Relic victory.

name: Mule Cart
description: A mobile drop site that takes wood, gold, stone and meat. It can drive to a new resource and moves to the nearest one by itself when its current site runs out. It researches the woodcutting and mining upgrades and can garrison inside buildings. Georgians start the game with one.

name: Outpost
description: A cheap lookout post that only gives line of sight. It cannot attack or hold units. Its vision grows with each age, from 6 tiles in the Dark Age to 12 in the Imperial Age.

name: Palisade Gate
description: A gate placed in a Palisade Wall. It opens for the player's own and allied units and stays shut to enemies, and it can be locked.

name: Palisade Wall
description: A cheap wooden wall that costs 3 wood per tile. It is weak but quick to build, and it slows raiders and blocks early rushes.

name: Pasture
description: The Khitan replacement for the Farm. Two Villagers can herd on a Pasture at the same time, and its central yurt is their drop site, so it works without a Mill. Like a Farm it runs out of food and has to be rebuilt.

name: Settlement
description: A drop site for all resources that also supports 5 population. It researches the farming, woodcutting and mining upgrades and unlocks Farms and the Market. A Settlement counts as two buildings for the Feudal Age requirement, and Mapuche Settlements can train the Spearman and Skirmisher lines.

name: Siege Workshop
description: Builds siege weapons: rams, Mangonels, Scorpions, Siege Towers and, in the Imperial Age, Bombard Cannons. The Cumans can build it in the Feudal Age.

name: Stable
requires: Feudal Age and a Barracks (or a Donjon for the Sicilians)
description: Trains and upgrades cavalry: the Scout line, Knights, Camels, Elephants and regional mounted units. It researches Bloodlines and Husbandry. The American civilizations cannot build it.

name: Stone Wall
description: A sturdier wall that costs 5 stone per tile. It holds much longer than Palisades and gains hit points in the Castle Age. The Fortified Wall technology at the University upgrades it.

name: Town Center
requires: Castle Age to build more than one (every player starts with one)
description: Every player starts with a Town Center. It trains Villagers, takes drop-offs of every resource, supports 5 population and researches the age advancements and early economy upgrades such as Loom and Wheelbarrow. An empty Town Center does not shoot, but garrisoned Villagers and archers make it fire arrows. Players can build extra Town Centers from the Castle Age onward, and they need flat ground.

name: University
description: Researches upgrades for buildings, towers, ranged units and ships, among them Masonry, Ballistics, Murder Holes, Chemistry and the ship upgrades Careening, Dry Dock and Shipwright. The tower and wall upgrades to Guard Tower, Keep, Bombard Tower and Fortified Wall are also researched here.

name: Watch Tower
description: The first tower that attacks. It shoots arrows at enemies in range, and garrisoned Villagers or archers add more arrows. Groups of Watch Towers are the basis of the tower rush.

name: Wonder
description: A huge monument that costs 1,000 wood, gold and stone. In standard games the player who completes a Wonder and keeps it standing for a set time wins. Every civilization has its own Wonder model, and it cannot be converted.
